statement: A physical quantity is a property of a phenomenon, body or substance that can be expressed by a number and a reference; a quantity value is the number-and-reference expression of its magnitude.
scope_limits: Áp dụng theo vocabulary metrology; 'reference' có thể là unit, procedure, material or combination.

statement: The SI is a coherent system of units founded on seven base units; derived SI units are formed as products of powers of base units with numerical factor one in coherent equations.
scope_limits: Mô tả cấu trúc SI, không ngụ ý mọi practical unit đều SI.

statement: Changing from one compatible unit to another changes the numerical value by the conversion factor but does not change the underlying quantity value.
scope_limits: Chỉ cho compatible quantities/units và exact/declared conversion factors.

statement: SI prefixes denote decimal powers attached to unit names/symbols according to SI rules and do not create new physical quantities.
scope_limits: Prefix rules có exceptions/format conventions; không dùng cho every non-SI unit.

statement: A measurement result must identify the measurand sufficiently and report a quantity value with unit/reference; bare numbers are generally not adequate for dimensional physical results.
scope_limits: Dimension-one quantities may legitimately use unit one or specialized dimensionless units.

statement: The dimension of a quantity expresses its dependence on base quantities as a product of powers and is independent of the particular unit chosen to express that quantity.
scope_limits: Dimension convention follows the chosen quantity system.

statement: A quantity equation is dimensionally homogeneous when the dimensions of terms related by equality or addition are compatible; this is a necessary consistency check.
scope_limits: Necessity does not imply physical truth.

statement: Quantities of dimension one can represent materially different concepts, so sharing dimension one does not make their meanings interchangeable.
scope_limits: E.g. ratios, angles, counts may need distinct semantic treatment.

statement: Unit conversion can be represented by multiplying by ratios equal to one, preserving dimension and quantity value while changing numerical representation.
scope_limits: Uses compatible units and valid conversion definitions.

statement: Dimensional analysis can rule out dimensionally inconsistent formulas but generally cannot determine dimensionless constants, signs, additive terms of same dimension, or prove a physical law.
scope_limits: Statement is a methodological limit, not a complete theory of Buckingham Pi or scaling.

statement: Measurement accuracy describes closeness of agreement between a measured quantity value and a true quantity value of a measurand; it is qualitative and is not itself a numerical quantity.
scope_limits: True quantity value is idealized/unknown in practice; accuracy is not uncertainty.

statement: Measurement precision describes closeness of agreement among indications or measured values obtained by replicate measurements under specified conditions.
scope_limits: Precision requires specified conditions and is commonly expressed through dispersion measures.

statement: Repeatability is precision under repeatability conditions, while reproducibility is precision under reproducibility conditions that deliberately vary specified conditions such as laboratories, operators or systems.
scope_limits: Exact condition sets must be declared for an evaluation.

statement: High precision does not guarantee high accuracy because a persistent systematic effect can shift a tightly clustered set of results away from a reference.
scope_limits: Reference comparison itself has uncertainty.

statement: Increasing display resolution or reporting more digits does not by itself demonstrate improved accuracy, precision or lower measurement uncertainty.
scope_limits: A valid claim about metrological quality requires evidence beyond display formatting.

statement: Measurement error is measured quantity value minus a reference quantity value, whereas measurement uncertainty is a non-negative parameter characterizing dispersion of quantity values attributed to the measurand.
scope_limits: Reference value and uncertainty framework must be stated; error is generally not exactly known.

statement: A systematic measurement error component remains constant or varies predictably in replicate measurements; a correction may compensate an estimated systematic effect but carries its own uncertainty.
scope_limits: Correction does not eliminate all residual uncertainty.

statement: A random measurement error component varies unpredictably in replicate measurements and contributes to dispersion; repetition can characterize but does not guarantee elimination of its contribution.
scope_limits: Random/systematic decomposition depends on model and conditions.

statement: Type A and Type B are methods for evaluating uncertainty components: Type A uses statistical analysis of measured values, while Type B uses other available information; they are not synonyms for random and systematic error.
scope_limits: Classification is by evaluation method.

statement: For a measurement model Y=f(X1,...,Xn), standard uncertainties can be propagated using sensitivity coefficients and covariance terms in the GUM framework; first-order linearized propagation can be inadequate for strong nonlinearity or non-Gaussian behavior.
scope_limits: Use suitable higher-order/numerical methods when linearization is inadequate.

statement: A measuring instrument is a device used for making measurements, alone or with supplementary devices; a measurement system is a set of elements assembled to perform specified measurements.
scope_limits: Definitions are generic and do not prescribe a particular sensor technology.

statement: An indication is the quantity value provided by a measuring instrument or system; it is not automatically identical to the final measurement result because corrections/model/uncertainty may be required.
scope_limits: Depends on measurement procedure and model.

statement: Resolution is the smallest change in a quantity being measured that causes a perceptible change in the corresponding indication; it is distinct from accuracy and total uncertainty.
scope_limits: Digital resolution may be display increment but total resolution can depend on system behavior.

statement: Sensitivity relates change in indication to change in the corresponding measured quantity value and can vary with operating point.
scope_limits: Local/functional definition depends on instrument characteristic.

statement: Calibration establishes, under specified conditions, a relation between standards' values with uncertainties and indications, then uses that relation to obtain a measurement result; calibration is not the same as adjustment.
scope_limits: Calibration may inform adjustment, but identity is false.

statement: A measurement standard is a realization of the definition of a given quantity with stated quantity value and associated uncertainty, used as a reference.
scope_limits: Standard may be artefact, instrument, reference material, system or defined realization.

statement: Metrological traceability is a property of a measurement result whereby it can be related to a reference through a documented unbroken chain of calibrations, each contributing to measurement uncertainty.
scope_limits: Traceability is result-specific and requires a stated reference.

statement: A calibration hierarchy is a sequence of calibrations from a reference through measurement systems, with associated uncertainties enabling traceability.
scope_limits: Hierarchy may have multiple levels/forms; it is not a guarantee of fitness.

statement: The SI is defined by fixing numerical values of seven defining constants; practical realization of SI units uses methods consistent with those definitions rather than relying on one unique artefact for every unit.
scope_limits: Realization methods can evolve while definitions remain fixed.

statement: Traceability to SI or another reference does not by itself prove a result is fit for a particular decision; uncertainty, method validity and required tolerance still matter.
scope_limits: Fitness-for-purpose depends on application-specific requirements.
